newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends steady, but market still jittery.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends steady, but market still jittery.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed almost unchanged on Monday after a day of consolidation following hefty losses last week, dealers said.
March Brent ended the session four cents up at $22.58 a barrel.
But dealers said the market remained volatile with thin volumes leaving it vulnerable to sharp moves on little fundamental news.
"We were seeing 40 to 50 cents moves last week and even today the market spiked up at one point without much behind it," said one broker.
March Brent hit a high of $22.91 a barrel in mid-afternoon trade as NYMEX crude made an upside break.
"(Brent) didn't quite hit resistance (at $22.94), but then it held well above (key technical support) at $22.00" said one dealer.

Brent fared better than gas oil which earlier closed sharply lower as forecasts for higher temperatures in the United States compounded already-bearish sentiment in Europe generated by mild weather conditions.
The March Brent/gas oil crack spread came under pressure to close at $4.47 a barrel.
Feb gas oil closed $6.75 a tonne lower at $209 having breached several support levels through the day.
"It was hovering around $3 to $4 down for most of the day and then slumped towards the end as (NYMEX) heating oil came off," a broker said.
Heating oil was trading over one cent a gallon lower at when the IPE gas oil trade closed, and ended its session nearly two cents down.
Temperatures on the U.S. East Coast and in the Midwest are expected to be above-normal this week, dampening heating oil demand.
Mild temperatures in Europe have stifled demand for heating oil barges in the ARA region, European physical traders said.
